Valuable Features
OpenText Functional Testing's most valuable features include expansive cross-platform and technology compatibility. Users appreciate its comprehensive support for GUI, API, mobile, web, and desktop applications. The ability to perform object identification, integrate with numerous third-party products, and utilize AI tools enhances ease of use. VBScript capability simplifies coding, while the inclusion of frameworks like BPT and LeanFT allows flexible test automation. Descriptive programming and object repository management streamline test development.

Room for Improvement
OpenText Functional Testing could improve by offering better browser compatibility and memory optimization. Object identification is not always reliable. Users seek improvements in performance consistency, especially during long executions. Integration with modern programming languages and support for cross-browser testing are desired, as well as expanded AI functionality and lower licensing costs. Users have noted challenges with the interface and technical support response times, expressing a need for enhanced reporting features and reduced dependency on specific scripting languages.

ROI
OpenText Functional Testing is highly regarded for enhancing productivity and efficiency through automation. Companies have experienced significant returns with reduced manual labor, cutting testing times by up to 80%, and increasing testing accuracy. Users report ROI over 300% in the long term and substantial cost savings through AI capabilities. Enterprise users find OpenText Functional Testing costly, with seat licenses around $10,000 and concurrent licenses approximately $17,000 including tax and maintenance. While priced higher than some alternatives, users acknowledge its comprehensive capabilities and integration with ALM/Quality Center. Many organizations opt for a mix of seat and concurrent licenses to manage costs effectively. Discounts and a variety of licensing options provide flexibility, though the model is perceived as complex and at times, confusing.

Learn more about OpenText Application Quality Management
Known for its robust reporting and flexibility, OpenText Application Quality Management is tailored for large organizations requiring a comprehensive solution supporting lifecycle coverage and seamless tool integration. Users can consolidate testing processes, manage requirements, and centralize reporting across manual and automated testing. While some face issues with project tracking, outdated interfaces, and limited browser compatibility beyond Internet Explorer, it remains widely used for regression and performance testing. Integration with tools like JIRA and support for tools such as UFT and ALM PC underscore its utility.
What are the key features of OpenText Application Quality Management?
Centralized Data Management: Consolidates and organizes testing data efficiently.
Traceability: Ensures traceability across all stages of the testing lifecycle.
Integration Capabilities: Connects seamlessly with automation and other essential tools.
Test Planning and Execution: Supports both manual and automated tests in a streamlined manner.
Advanced Reporting: Provides robust options to generate insightful test reports.
Customization: Offers tailored solutions to fit specific organizational needs.
What benefits should users look for in reviews?
Efficiency: Increases test management efficiency across projects.
Scalability: Adapts to the varying scope of large-scale projects.
Lifecycle Coverage: Comprehensive management from requirement to defect tracking.
User-Friendly Interface: Designed for ease of use despite needing updates.
Cost-Effectiveness: Balances high initial costs with long-term savings through efficient testing management.
In industries such as finance and healthcare, OpenText Application Quality Management is implemented to ensure rigorous testing standards. It supports test case creation and execution, defect tracking, and requirements management. Integration with JIRA and performance testing tools make it suitable for organizations needing synchronized testing environments.
OpenText Application Quality Management was previously known as Micro Focus ALM Quality Center, HPE ALM, Quality Center, Quality Center, Micro Focus ALM, OpenText Quality Manager.
